_comment: PACES (Physical Activity Enjoyment Scale) catalog onboarding. Source: Kendzierski, D., & DeCarlo, K. J. (1991). Physical Activity Enjoyment Scale: Two validation studies. Journal of Sport & Exercise Psychology, 13(1), 50-64. Original 18-item bipolar/semantic-differential scale, each item a pair of opposite statements anchored by a 7-point numeric scale (1-7); respondent circles the number between the two poles that best matches how they feel about the physical activity right now. 11 items are reverse-scored for the final sum (range 18-126): items 1,4,5,7,9,10,11,13,14,16,17. Item wording, order and the reverse-scored item list were cross-checked against two independent secondary sources reproducing the full original English scale (consistent with each other and internally self-consistent with the polarity of each stated pole pair).

study.title: Physical Activity Enjoyment Scale (PACES) - Instrument Onboarding
study.objective: Register the PACES instrument and its physical-activity-enjoyment dimension into the GDX_HUMAN psychometric catalog as reusable knowledge for future exercise-psychology studies.
study.method: Desk research of the published instrument (Kendzierski & DeCarlo, 1991) and secondary validation literature; catalog registration only, no primary data collection associated with this record.

instruments.name: Physical Activity Enjoyment Scale (PACES)
instruments.description: Kendzierski, D., & DeCarlo, K. J. (1991). Physical Activity Enjoyment Scale: Two validation studies. Journal of Sport & Exercise Psychology, 13(1), 50-64.
instruments.instructions: Please rate how you feel at the moment about the physical activity you have been doing. For each pair of statements below, circle the number from 1 to 7 that best represents how you feel right now, with each end of the scale (1 and 7) corresponding to the statement shown at that end.
instruments.phenomenon_description: The pattern of affective and psychological responses -- positive well-being, psychological distress, and fatigue -- that individuals report during or immediately after a bout of physical exercise.

constructs.name: Physical Activity Enjoyment (PACES)
constructs.definition: The degree of pleasure and positive affect that an individual derives from engaging in a specific bout of physical activity or exercise.

variables.name: Physical Activity Enjoyment (PACES)
variables.description: Overall enjoyment reported by the respondent in relation to the physical activity/exercise just performed or being performed.
variables.operational_definition: Sum of the 18 PACES items (each rated 1-7), after reverse-scoring items 1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16 and 17.
variables.indicator_description: Sum of the 18 PACES items, each rated 1-7, with the 11 reverse-scored items inverted before summing.
